en: Coconut oil is a solid in air-conditioned rooms but melts into a clear liquid under the hot Philippine sun.
Halo-halo is a heterogeneous mixture because you can easily see and physically separate its different ingredients like beans and jelly.
Seawater in Manila Bay is a homogeneous solution because the dissolved salt is evenly mixed and invisible in the water.
Frosted glass windows in local bakeries are translucent because they scatter light, allowing you to see shapes but not distinct details.
Iron roofs rust faster in humid coastal towns like Tacloban because moisture and salt trigger a chemical change.
Honey poured over hot pandesal flows slower than water because it has a higher viscosity.
Pumice stones from Taal Volcano can float on water because their overall density is lower than liquid water.
Water vapor from boiling sinigang condenses into tiny liquid droplets on the cold kitchen ceiling, showing a state change.
Muddy water from the Pasig River after heavy rain is a suspension because heavy soil particles eventually settle.
Tearing a piece of banana leaf into smaller strips is a physical change because the material's chemical identity remains the same.
Brown sugar dissolves faster in hot kapeng barako than in cold water because higher temperatures increase the solubility.
Calamansi juice tastes sour and turns blue litmus paper red because it contains citric acid, showing its chemical property.
